title: Cross-engine QA: token drift, compact controls, and table overflow on Safari/Firefox + mobile
creator: Aisha Romero
description: Audit and triage a set of cross-engine regressions discovered during the mobile and Safari/Firefox QA sweep. Focus areas: design token drift between compiled CSS and component runtime, compact button hit-area regressions in dense lists, table cell wrapping & overflow with variable token scales, and chart legend truncation on small viewports. Goal is to produce reproducible issues, prioritize fixes with engineering, and update the UI kit tokens/guidelines so regressions don't recur.
acceptance_criteria: All reproducible issues captured with clear steps and screenshot artifacts
Severity classification for each finding and high-priority items assigned to engineering
Patch guidance or token mapping provided for each regression (token name -> expected value)
Design system docs updated with a short 'cross-engine gotchas' checklist
Follow-up tasks created for engineering changes, tests, or token migrations
steps_to_reproduce: Open Figma reference frame 'Buttons / Compact' and compare computed styles in Safari (macOS 14) and Firefox 122 with component in Storybook running latest main
Set system font scaling to 125% on macOS and inspect button hit targets in dense list (Inbox sample) — note any < 44px hit area
Load the example 'Table / Responsive' with variable token scale (compact, default, spacious) and narrow viewport (320px) — observe cell wrap and horizontal scroll behavior
Mount the 'Chart / Legend' example in mobile emulator (iOS 17 Safari) and toggle small-legend mode — capture truncation and overlapping labels
Compare CSS variables used by runtime to Figma token exports (colors, spacing, typography) using the token-export CSV
progress_updates: 2026-02-26: Kicked off sweep focused on Safari and Firefox. Found button hit-area regressions in dense list variant and inconsistent token values for spacing-xs.
2026-03-02: Confirmed token mismatch originates from compiled token map used by build step. Not a runtime bug in most cases — needs token remap and one-off legacy token aliasing.
2026-03-06: Captured reproducible table overflow cases with 3rd-party virtualized table; filed initial ENG spike to reproduce in isolation (ENG-5124).
2026-03-10: Prioritized three P0/P1 fixes: token alias remapping, compact-button hit-area increase, and table min-width guard. Assigned ENG owners and blocked on a small CSS patch review.
2026-03-14: Eng PR merged for token aliasing. Design review: confirm no visual regressions in spacious layout before closing this ticket.
review_feedback: PM (Nora Patel): Prefer minimal visual change; where possible prefer token aliasing over changing component CSS to avoid downstream UX variance.
Engineering (Diego Morales): Suggested a short-term runtime shim to reconcile legacy tokens, and a follow-up to remove the shim after client apps migrate.
Accessibility (Priya Anand): Increase compact button hit areas to at least 40px and ensure focus ring is visible in high-contrast mode.
notes: Trade-off: increasing compact button hit area may slightly change layout density in some legacy screens; recommended to scope change to components flagged 'density: compact' only.
Longer-term: add visual regression tests across Safari/Firefox to the UI kit CI matrix and include token parity checks against the canonical token export.
Follow-up tasks: create an ENG task to add end-to-end Storybook snapshots on macOS Safari headless in CI, and a design task to document token alias deprecation schedule.
